headline: Majors hold above 200s with weakening momentum; whales rotating onto exchanges while ETF bid persists; BNB overheating while alts diverge.
paragraphs: Regime is intact but tired. All seven majors sit above their 200-day simple moving average, a clean bull structure. However, momentum is failing to push through. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and Doge all show MACD below signal line, meaning the fast momentum has rolled below the slow momentum. Only BNB stands apart, with MACD above signal and RSI at 78.1, genuinely overbought on the day, up 5.96 percent. The regime still reads bullish in trend, but the gas is leaking out of the pedal. Golden crosses (the 50-day above the 200-day) confirm the structure for Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB, a solid foundation. Bitcoin and Doge lack the cross, though Bitcoin is well above the 200. The tension is clear: price has climbed hard this month (Bitcoin up 24.4 percent, Ethereum 32.2 percent, Solana 39.6 percent, BNB 35.4 percent), but the acceleration is stalling even as the crowd feels giddy at 73 on the fear and greed index, near the top of its 30-day range of 27 to 74.

Positioning in perpetuals is crowded and mixed, with some leverage fleeing. Bitcoin funding is negative at minus 0.0042 percent per eight hours, annualizing to minus 4.6 percent, meaning shorts are paying longs to hold the bet. The trade is expensive to be long. Ethereum funding sits nearly flat at minus 0.0002 percent, essentially cost-free, while Solana is also short-paying at minus 3.3 percent. Only XRP and Doge have positive funding, with XRP at 1.1 percent annualized and Doge at 2.7 percent, but those are smaller venues. Open interest remains substantial across the board: Bitcoin 2.15 billion, Ethereum 1.48 billion, Solana 298 million. Liquidations over the last 20-24 hours tell a layered story. Bitcoin saw 100 liquidations, with shorts hit 5 times harder than longs (300K shorts versus 58K longs). Ethereum liquidations were balanced (255K longs, 235K shorts). Solana skewed short (102K versus 65K). XRP and Doge, by contrast, saw sharp long liquidations (Doge especially: 403K shorts to 194K longs). The message is fragmented: no overwhelming squeeze in either direction, but pockets of overleveraged euphoria, particularly in smaller-cap leveraged plays.

Whale flows confirm the mixed posture. Over the last 24 hours, 135 million dollars moved onto exchanges, net, a swing toward selling pressure. Bitcoin alone saw 80.9 million net onto exchanges: large inflows to Coinbase Institutional (369 million combined) offset by cold storage withdrawals (466 million). Ethereum saw 54.2 million net onto exchanges with zero outflows, a pure inflow to the spot market. Yet the weekly picture differs. Week ending September 5 shows 493.6 million moved off exchanges, a reversal from the prior three weeks, which all saw heavy onto-exchange flows (573 million, 1.125 billion, 596 million). The current week's flip is notable: it suggests long-term holders or institutions may be reclaiming coins. Stablecoin float sits at 310.5 billion, up 1.49 percent over 30 days, flat for the window in question. The dry powder is not accumulating aggressively, and the recent onto-exchange movement coupled with a weekly off-exchange move hints at repositioning rather than new capital entering.

ETF flows from traditional finance continue to bid into spot. Bitcoin ETF saw inflows of 174.6 million on September 4, with the last five sessions netting 986.7 million, all in the same direction for three of the last five days. Ethereum saw 25.9 million inflow on the day and 215.3 million over five sessions, though only two days moved the same direction. Cumulative BTC ETF flows stand at 55.7 billion; Ethereum at 13.2 billion. This is genuine institutional demand, steady and substantial. It undercuts the idea of a peak-euphoria flush; traditional money is still buying. However, the five-session rate (Bitcoin roughly 200 million per day, Ethereum 43 million per day) is not extreme, and Ethereum's directional consistency is weaker than Bitcoin's.

Ethereum presents a real divergence worth watching. Price is up 0.14 percent on the day but down 1.86 percent over seven days, yet up 32.2 percent over thirty days. MACD sits below signal, RSI is 62.9 (neutral), and distance from the 12-month high is deep at minus 47.8 percent. The month-long rally is real, but the weekly pullback in the face of rising ETF bids suggests some profit taking or weakness beneath the surface. BNB is the opposite: 5.96 percent on the day, up 8.05 percent on the week, 35.4 percent over thirty days, MACD above signal, and RSI at 78.1. It is the only major running hot. The 24-hour moves mask a bifurcation: quality momentum in a handful of assets, fatigue in most others.

Watch for three tells of a regime shift: funding that flips decisively positive across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana at the same time (a sign of renewed long crowding and cost acceleration); Bitcoin reclaiming a golden cross (50-day above 200-day) to confirm that the slower trend is still climbing; or sustained stablecoin float declines paired with off-exchange whale moves (a sign that dry powder is shrinking while demand is real). Until then, the structure holds, but the engine needs to prove it still has revolutions left.
